construction_description: Annotators identify the long answer by selecting the smallest HTML bounding box that contains all information required to answer the question, on a Wikipedia page provided from top search results.

A relation template is sampled and instantiated into a relational requirement over the knowledge base; the gold answer is a candidate node satisfying that requirement. Three models verify candidates, and only candidates passing all three enter the final ground-truth answer set.
Factual sentences are extracted from news articles by a trained language model; the gold evidence is these source-text sentences paired with article metadata. No knowledge graph is used.
The core component is the inferential chain representing the relation between the topic entity and the answer in Freebase; the gold semantic parse encodes this chain with Freebase identifiers.

Crowd workers write questions over pairs of linked Wikipedia paragraphs and explicitly mark the sentence-level supporting facts they used to answer; the construction explicitly rejects a knowledge graph and focuses on text-based question answering.

Composed bottom-up from human-annotated single-hop questions drawn from five English Wikipedia-based reading-comprehension datasets; the supporting paragraph for each hop is the annotated paragraph carried over from the source dataset. No knowledge graph is used; a disconnection filter and an anti-leakage split are applied.

Query requirements include textual properties extracted from the gold node's free text; this axis is knowledge-base node free-text rather than the relational structure, fused into the query by a language model.

Logic Mining transforms raw text into structured domain ontologies; evidence is isolated into localized subgraphs mined from the corpus, and questions are generated according to the complexity of the underlying evidence, combined with human checking for final confirmation.

Sentence-level supporting facts are sentence indices found by a heuristic that checks whether the Wikidata object value appears in the Wikipedia article for the entity; the knowledge-graph value is projected onto text, while the sentence surface itself is Wikipedia text.
The answer must be a short span quoted verbatim from the passage, enforced by a deterministic gate; the knowledge graph is never provided in the prompt, with a static import guard.

Questions are created from predefined templates by replacing template tokens with entity labels, using logical-rule information in the knowledge graph; the answer is the object entity of the Wikidata logical rule.
The canonical gold edge identifier is written directly from the knowledge-graph triple in the form source--relation-->target; overlap with the knowledge graph is total by construction.

Source articles are split into text chunks and embedded; supporting evidence traces back to original source documents. The chunks serving as gold for a question are selected by guidance from the question's path and answer, while the chunk text itself is source text.
Question-answer pairs are authored independently by trivia enthusiasts, before and independently of evidence gathering.

Shortest directed acyclic paths of length 2 to 5 are enumerated within a knowledge graph; the unique answer is the terminal node of the path, and all supporting facts are contained in the edge set of the graph. A semantic-clustering augmentation adds links beyond the original graph.

Evidence documents are gathered after the fact and retained for a question when they contain the answer string; the construction states that the presence of the answer string in an evidence document implies that the document answers the question.
The answer text is built by filling a textual template with a knowledge-graph edge's relation phrase and its context field; no language model is involved.
SPARQL queries with standard Freebase entity identifiers are provided and are directly executable on Freebase; the gold answers are the Freebase entities returned by executing the parse.
The short answer is one or more entities, or a boolean, selected by a human annotator as a span on the Wikipedia page.
The answer is a span written by the crowd worker over the Wikipedia paragraph text; no knowledge graph is involved in construction.

A generator model receives only raw corpus passage text; the evidence span is an exact substring of the passage. The knowledge graph is never provided in the prompt, and a static import guard forbids the generation pipeline from importing any knowledge-graph code.

Questions are generated by aligning their cognitive demands with the structural properties of the underlying evidence subgraph; the answer is anchored to the mined subgraph with its surface present in text, and human checking is applied.
Evidence is a set of triples, each a structured datum of subject entity, property, and object entity, obtained from the Wikidata.
The expected gold entities are the two endpoint node identifiers of a knowledge-graph edge, copied directly from the evaluation knowledge graph by code.

The answer is the human-annotated answer of the composed question's final hop, inherited from the source single-hop datasets; a disconnection filter rejects questions answerable without all hops. No knowledge graph is used.
Claims are paraphrased from article sentences by GPT-4, which then composes a query whose answer is grounded in the source claims; a subset is manually reviewed. No knowledge graph is used.
The gold path is the pair of endpoint node identifiers of the knowledge-graph edge, copied from the evaluation knowledge graph.
The gold reasoning path is a sequence of knowledge-graph triples; the 2-hop and 3-hop subsets are generated from the same knowledge base by relation-chain traversal.
All questions are generated from a movie knowledge base using question templates; the answer is the tail entity reached by traversing the knowledge-graph reasoning path.
